subject: English
passage:
The following text is from Jennifer Egan's 2010 novel A Visit from the Goon Squad.

Last summer my grandmother decided to give me her antique jewelry box from when she moved to Florida. She wrapped it beautifully and presented it to me on my birthday. I smiled widely and thanked her because she seemed so proud of the gift, but honestly I couldn't stand the sight of it from the moment she placed it on my dresser. The jewelry box stared back at me with its tiny mirror. It was like a museum piece that belonged somewhere else, not cluttering up my space.

©2010 by Jennifer Egan
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: It explains why the narrator always wanted her grandmother's jewelry box on her dresser.
choices.B: It suggests that the narrator's grandmother is an experienced gift wrapper.
choices.C: It describes the circumstances that led the narrator's grandmother to move to Florida.
choices.D: It establishes how the narrator feels about the jewelry box.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it best states the main purpose of the text, which is to establish the narrator's feelings about the jewelry box. The narrator reveals that she "smiled widely and thanked her" grandmother even though she "honestly couldn't stand the sight of it" from the moment it was placed on her dresser. The narrator also describes the jewelry box as staring back at her and compares it to a museum piece that doesn't belong in her space. These details establish the narrator's feelings about the jewelry box, suggesting that it makes her uncomfortable.
